reading.title: Bioluminescence in Deep-Sea Organisms
reading.passage: Bioluminescence, the production of light by living organisms, represents one of the most fascinating adaptations in marine biology. Approximately 90 percent of deep-sea creatures exhibit some form of bioluminescence, utilizing this capability for diverse purposes including predation, communication, and defense. The chemical reaction occurs when a protein called luciferin reacts with oxygen in specialized cells known as photophores, resulting in the emission of light with minimal energy loss. In the perpetually dark abyssal zone where sunlight cannot penetrate, this mechanism has evolved as an indispensable survival strategy. For instance, the anglerfish employs a bioluminescent lure to attract prey, while certain jellyfish species utilize light emission as a warning signal to potential predators. Recent research has revealed that approximately 80 percent of bioluminescent organisms produce blue or green light, wavelengths that transmit most efficiently through seawater. This biochemical phenomenon not only demonstrates the remarkable adaptability of life in extreme environments but also provides valuable insights into enzyme function and marine ecosystem dynamics that scientists continue to investigate.

questions.q: According to the passage, approximately what percentage of deep-sea creatures use bioluminescence?
options: 60 percent
80 percent
90 percent
95 percent
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 번째 문장에서 '약 90%의 심해 생물들이 생물발광의 어떤 형태를 드러낸다'고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the efficiency of blue and green light in seawater?
options: They are the only colors that can be produced by organisms
They transmit through seawater better than other wavelengths
They require less energy to produce than other colors
They are primarily used for long-distance communication
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '약 80%의 생물발광 생물이 파란색 또는 녹색 빛을 생성한다'는 것은 '이 파장이 해수를 통해 가장 효율적으로 전송된다'는 이유로 설명됩니다.

questions.q: The word 'indispensable' in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: common
essential
temporary
unusual

questions.q: Why does the author mention the anglerfish as an example?
options: To explain why deep-sea creatures cannot see natural light
To show how bioluminescence is used for different purposes in marine life
To describe the most common type of bioluminescent organism
To argue that bioluminescence is more important than other adaptations
questions.explanation: 저자는 생물발광이 포식, 의사소통, 방어 등 다양한 목적으로 사용된다고 설명하며, 아귀의 예시는 생물발광이 포식을 위해 어떻게 사용되는지 보여줍니다.

speaking.prompt: Some people believe students should freely choose their major based on personal interest. Others think students should choose majors that have better job prospects. Which approach do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and examples.
model_sentences: I believe students should have the freedom to choose their major based on their personal interests rather than focusing solely on job prospects.
First, when students study subjects they are passionate about, they are more motivated and likely to perform better academically, which ultimately benefits their careers.
For example, if a student loves biology and becomes a marine biologist, their genuine enthusiasm helps them conduct better research and contribute meaningfully to their field.
Additionally, pursuing your passion leads to greater job satisfaction and reduces the likelihood of career burnout in the long run.
Therefore, while job prospects are important, personal interest should be the primary factor in choosing a major.

listening.title: Psychology Lecture: The Formation of Memory
listening.script: Professor: Good morning, everyone. Today we're going to discuss one of the most fundamental processes in psychology—memory formation. So, how does memory actually work? Well, memory formation involves three main stages: encoding, consolidation, and retrieval. During encoding, sensory information is processed and converted into a form that the brain can store. The second stage, consolidation, is when this information is actually transferred from short-term memory to long-term memory. This process typically requires sleep, which is why studying before an exam might be less effective than studying several days before. Finally, retrieval is when we access stored information. Now, I want to emphasize something important: memories are not fixed records like video recordings. Instead, they're reconstructive. Every time you remember something, you're actually rebuilding that memory based on scattered neural traces. This reconstruction process can introduce errors, which is why eyewitness testimony isn't always reliable. What questions do you have about these stages?

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 정보를 저장 가능한 형태로 변환하는 과정
신경 흔적, 뇌 속의 기억 흔적

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
options: The differences between short-term and long-term memory
The three stages of memory formation and how memory works
Why sleep is important for studying before exams
The history of memory research in psychology
questions.explanation: 교수가 기억 형성의 세 단계(인코딩, 공고화, 인출)를 설명하고 기억의 재구성적 특성을 강조하므로 기억 형성과 그 작동 원리가 강의의 주요 주제입니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, why might studying the night before an exam be less effective than studying days earlier?
options: Because you will be too tired to focus
Because consolidation requires sleep to transfer information to long-term memory
Because short-term memory can hold less information at night
Because the brain forgets information faster in the evening
questions.explanation: 교수는 공고화 단계에서 정보가 단기 기억에서 장기 기억으로 옮겨지는 데 보통 수면이 필요하다고 설명하므로, 시험 전날 밤에 공부하는 것이 며칠 전에 공부하는 것보다 효과가 떨어질 수 있습니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor mention that memories are reconstructive rather than fixed recordings?
options: To explain why memory encoding requires more effort than other processes
To illustrate that memories can contain errors and inaccuracies when retrieved
To demonstrate why consolidation is the most important stage of memory formation
To show that long-term memory is more reliable than short-term memory
questions.explanation: 교수는 기억이 재구성되며 매번 기억할 때마다 신경 흔적을 기반으로 재구축되므로 오류가 발생할 수 있다고 설명하며, 목격자 증언이 항상 신뢰할 수 없는 이유를 제시합니다.
